text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.35% today as U.S. refineries continue running at exceptionally high capacity (97.4%), a level that typically supports strong margins for a major refiner. The backdrop remains geopolitical tension in the Middle East—particularly around the Strait of Hormuz—where tanker attacks and Iran–U.S. friction have kept oil prices elevated ($83.90/barrel domestically, $88.24 globally), though today's move was modest and the stock has been volatile this week, swinging down 2.2% yesterday before recovering today.

The refining sector is benefiting from persistent supply disruptions and global energy market tightness; Europe's gas storage is historically low heading into winter, and Middle East LNG flows remain disrupted, keeping international energy demand and prices firm. This structural strength in refining conditions has supported the stock's 2% gain over two weeks despite daily swings.
